subject: physics
title: Static electricity
key_idea: Rubbing two insulators together transfers electrons from one to the other. The one that gains electrons is negative and the one that loses them is positive. Like charges repel and unlike charges attract.

blocks.text: When certain insulating materials are rubbed together, they become electrically charged. This section covers how.

items.meaning: A material that does not conduct. Static charge only builds up on insulators.
A negatively charged particle. Electrons are the only charges that move.
Connecting an object to the ground with a conductor so that excess charge can flow away.

items: Most objects have equal numbers of positive and negative charges, so their effects cancel and the net charge is zero.
Rubbing makes electrons move from one material to the other.
The material that gains electrons becomes negatively charged.
The material that loses electrons is left with an equal positive charge.

diagram.alt: Put the steps of charging a plastic rod by rubbing it with a cloth into the right order.
steps: A plastic rod is rubbed with a cloth.
Friction transfers electrons from the cloth to the rod.
The rod gains electrons, so it becomes negatively charged.
The cloth loses electrons, so it is left with an equal positive charge.

blocks.text: Only electrons move. Any mention of positive charges or positive electrons moving scores no marks.

items: Friction transfers electrons between insulators.
Gaining electrons gives a negative charge. Losing electrons leaves an equal positive charge.
Only negative electrons move, never positive charges.

blocks.text: When two charged objects are brought close together, they exert a force on each other without touching. This is a non-contact force.

items: Two objects with the same type of charge repel.
Two objects with different types of charge attract.

diagram.alt: Sort each pair of objects into attract or repel.

items.text: A positive rod and a negative rod
Strands of hair that all have the same charge
A positively charged comb and a piece of paper
A negatively charged balloon and a positively charged cloth

items: Two charged balloons hung on strings move apart if they have the same type of charge.
A charged comb picks up small pieces of paper.
A student's hair stands on end when each hair has the same charge.

blocks.text: Why a charged object attracts a neutral one

items: A charged comb brought near paper induces an opposite charge on the part of the paper closest to the comb.
Opposite charges attract, so the paper is pulled to the comb.
A charged balloon sticks to a wall in the same way, because of induced charges in the wall.
Like charges repel. Unlike charges attract. Both are non-contact forces.
A charged object induces the opposite charge on the nearest part of a neutral object, so it attracts it.

blocks.text: Charge can build up on an object and then flow away. This section covers sparks, earthing, uses and dangers.

items: A charged object has a potential difference to an earthed conductor.
When they are close enough, electrons transfer between them and a spark jumps.
A negatively charged student who touches a metal tap gets a shock. Electrons transfer from the student to the tap, which earths the charge.
Lightning is a spark between a charged cloud and the ground.
Earthing removes excess charge by the movement of electrons through a conductor to earth.
A carpet with thin copper wires is a conductor, so charge does not build up on a person.
Charge can build up as fuel flows through a pipe when refuelling a car or an aeroplane.
A spark could ignite the flammable fuel and cause a fire or explosion.
The pipe and the vehicle are connected by a metal wire to earth, so they are at the same potential and no charge builds up.
Insecticide and disinfectant sprayers give each droplet the same charge.
The droplets repel each other and spread out.
They are attracted to the surface, including parts not in the direct line of the spray.
Electrostatic dust precipitators use static electricity to remove smoke particles from factory chimneys.
A spark is electrons moving across a gap because of a large potential difference.
Earthing lets electrons flow away, so no dangerous charge builds up.
Charged sprayer droplets repel each other and are attracted to the surface.

checks.q: A plastic rod is rubbed with a cloth and becomes negatively charged. Explain why the cloth becomes positively charged.
checks.a: Electrons are transferred from the cloth to the rod. Electrons are negatively charged, so the cloth has more positive charges than negative charges.

checks.q: What force acts between two negatively charged rods?
checks.a: A force of repulsion, because they have the same charge.

checks.q: Explain how earthing a metal pipe reduces the danger of sparks when refuelling.
checks.a: The pipe is connected to earth by a conductor. Electrons flow through it to earth, so no charge builds up and there is no spark to ignite the fuel.

exam_phrases: electrons transferred from the cloth (to the rod)
electrons are negatively charged
there are more positive charges than negative charges on the cloth
there is a potential difference between the student and the tap
which causes electrons / charges to transfer from the student
a force of repulsion
the rods have the same charge

mistakes.wrong: Positive charge is transferred from the rod to the cloth.
mistakes.right: Any mention of the transfer of positive charge scores 0. Only electrons move.

mistakes.wrong: The student gets a shock because the tap is charged.
mistakes.right: The tap is not charged. The tap is earthed. There is a potential difference between the student and the tap, so electrons transfer.

mistakes.wrong: The cloth is positive because it has gained positive electrons.
mistakes.right: There are no positive electrons. The cloth lost electrons, so it has more positive charges than negative charges.

worked_example.question: A student rubbed a plastic rod with a cloth. The rod became negatively charged and the cloth became positively charged. Explain why the cloth became positively charged.
answer_points: Electrons are transferred from the cloth (to the rod).
So there are more positive charges than negative charges on the cloth.
worked_example.tip: The second mark only scores if it is linked to the first: the electrons must move from the cloth.

exam_phrases: friction (between cloth and comb)
transfer of electrons / charge
electrons carry a negative charge
leaving excess positive charge on the comb
a negative charge is induced on the part of the paper closest to the comb
opposite charges attract
electrons / negative charges move down the wire / to earth

mistakes.wrong: Positive electrons move from the comb to the cloth.
mistakes.right: Reference to positive electrons or positive charge moving loses the mark. Electrons carry a negative charge and move from the comb to the cloth.

mistakes.wrong: The comb picks up paper because the paper is positive.
mistakes.right: Explain induction: a negative charge is induced on the part of the paper closest to the comb, and opposite charges attract.

mistakes.wrong: When the spark jumps, positive charges move down the wire to earth.
mistakes.right: Reject positive charge moving. Electrons (negative charges) move down the wire to earth.

worked_example.question: A student rubs a plastic comb with a dry cloth to give the comb a positive electric charge. Explain how rubbing the comb with a dry cloth gives the comb a positive electric charge.
answer_points: Friction between the cloth and the comb.
Electrons are transferred from the comb on to the cloth.
This leaves an excess positive charge on the comb.
worked_example.tip: Link any three of the four points. Do not write about positive electrons or positive charge moving.

exam_phrases: equal numbers of protons and electrons
so the effects of positive charges and negative charges cancel out
electrons are transferred
different numbers of protons and electrons
negative charges / electrons can move
rub the balloon (against the cloth)

mistakes.right: Negative charges, the electrons, can move.

mistakes.wrong: The ruler becomes charged because protons move from the cloth.
mistakes.right: Protons and positive charges do not move and are not accepted. Electrons are transferred, so the numbers of positive and negative charges are no longer equal.

mistakes.wrong: A plastic ruler is not charged because it has no charges.
mistakes.right: It has equal numbers of protons and electrons, so the effects of the positive and negative charges cancel out.

worked_example.question: A student investigates static electricity using a plastic ruler. Explain in terms of electrons why the ruler becomes charged when the student rubs it with a cloth.
answer_points: Electrons are transferred between the ruler and the cloth (electrons are lost or gained).
The charges are no longer equal, so the effects no longer cancel out.
worked_example.tip: One mark for the transfer of electrons and one for the charges no longer being equal. Do not say that protons or positive charges move.
